wave: measure the continuation state contract before VIEW-1 changes it
frozen: 2026-09-25, against main 0aae2cea (the CONTINUATION-PLUGIN-1 merge train complete: C6 #545 merged)
status: FORECAST — frozen before implementation; the execution record goes in continuation-mem-1-notes.json and this file is not edited
question: What continuation bytes exist, which of them are read, when are they read, and what does the current API force into existence that nothing needs?
why: CONTINUATION-PLUGIN-1 proved the continuation plane is open: named, selected, authority-carrying, external, dynamically loaded. C5 then met the read contract (`keys(layer) -> &[Vec<f32>]`, every row from position 0) as a concrete limit: a contiguous-buffer provider is inexpressible without opening it. VIEW-1 would open it. This programme measures the state first, so VIEW-1 changes what is PROVEN costly rather than what looks inelegant. The inventory (`docs/continuation-mem-1-inventory.md`) states the suspects from the code; MEM-1 prices them in bytes.

baseline.code: main 0aae2cea — CONTINUATION-PLUGIN-1 C6 (#545) merged; the last wave of the merge train

facts.read_contract: keys/values return &[Vec<f32>]: every appended row, from position 0, one heap allocation per row
facts.row_dtype: f32 everywhere; row length = kv_dim = num_kv_heads * head_dim

providers.row/v1: Vec<Vec<f32>> per layer, rows moved in
providers.canonical/v1: Array2 matrix per layer AND a Vec<Vec<f32>> view per layer

rule: MEASUREMENT ONLY. No production code changes in this programme. Every suspect in the inventory is priced, none is fixed here: a fix is either VIEW-1 (the read contract) or its own frozen perf rung, chosen from MEM-1's ranking.

subjects.mechanism: the in-tree fixtures that isolate one operator each: dense softmax, the sliding-window fixture (miniature_glimmer, crosses its window), and the KDA+MLA hybrid. No in-tree conv-QKV model fixture exists (only geometry-level tests), so conv-QKV mechanism AND magnitude are both measured on oute-mamba2attn-250m, the smallest real subject. Mechanism counts are exact on fixtures; magnitudes are NOT claimed from them (synthetic substrates misprice magnitude).

magnitude.sliding window: gemma3-4b-it.vindex3 (sequence longer than its window, so dead rows exist)
magnitude.KDA + MLA: Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct.s7.vindex3 (the accepted re-encode; .s6 is the declared latent-norm refusal fixture and is excluded). Short sequences only: its cost profile is the point, not throughput

subjects.geometry_is_read_not_assumed: every run records the plan's per-layer LayerContinuationGeometry (kind, kv_dim, window, latent width, recurrent buffer bytes); forecasts are evaluated against that record, never against remembered model cards

phases: resumed prefill (state already at position p; the server's chained turn)
handoff: ContinuationHandoff seal → ResponseKvCache insert → take → resume

instruments.I1_measuring_provider: `Measured<P: ContinuationProvider>` in a test/bench target (no trait change). Delegates every method and records per call: method, layer, phase, rows offered (slice length), and the capacity and pointer of each moved-in row.
instruments.I1_scoped_allocator: A counting #[global_allocator] in the measuring binary. While a scope is active on the owner thread it counts allocations, frees, sizes, and reallocations with their old/new addresses. Scope protocol, allocation-free inside: enter → snapshot atomic counters → delegated operation → snapshot → leave → only then record/format. The recorder never allocates while a scope is open.
instruments.I1_thread_integrity: a GLOBAL 'scope active' flag beside the thread-local attribution: any allocation on a thread other than the scope's owner while any scope is active marks the run INVALID. Together with every provider call recording one thread id, this proves thread-local accounting saw everything rather than assuming it.
instruments.I4_interval_scope_convqkv: ConvQkv's history copy happens in the executor between the provider's `values(layer)` returning and its next call (`recurrent_state(layer)`), both of which the wrapper sees. The wrapper opens an interval scope when `values` returns on a conv-QKV layer and closes it at the next provider entry. Allocations in that interval are classified by signature: row-sized (kv_dim × 4) allocations are copied history rows; the outer Vec is the list. Reconciled against h (the rows the provider held when the interval opened).
instruments.I5_counting_projections_mla: `mla_forward_with` (public) takes `projections: &dyn DenseProjections`. On the mechanism subject (the KDA+MLA hybrid) the harness drives the operator with a counting DenseProjections that records each call's (in_dim, out_dim); kv_b_proj calls are the ones shaped (kv_lora_rank → heads·(nope+v_head_dim)). The production projection ledger has no MLA site (sites: Recurrent, Ffn, Attention, Unclassified), so on the real Kimi subject decompressions are NOT independently observable without a production change: there the run records latent rows offered per call and the count is taken from the mechanism measurement plus the plan's geometry, stated as such.
instruments.I2_output_dependency_witness: renamed from 'read witness': perturbation establishes OUTPUT DEPENDENCE, not physical memory access. Perturb one held row outside the kernel's selected range → bit-identical logits required; perturb one inside it → a change required, with the perturbation sized to the row's own scale (a ULP of a large cell, never of zero).
instruments.I3_phase_harness: drives each subject through the four phases under row/v1 and canonical/v1 from the same registry, with bit-identical outputs asserted (the C3 parity gate), so byte differences are attributable to storage alone
instruments.I6_storage_identity: for handoff: the addresses and capacities of every backing allocation (K/V rows, matrix storage, latent rows, recurrent buffers) captured before seal and after resume

metrics.rows_offered_per_step: MEASURED at the provider boundary: slice length lent by keys/values
metrics.kernel_selected_range: STRUCTURAL FACT recorded per call from the execution's position and the layer's window (start..=position); not a measurement of memory reads
metrics.causal_boundary: I2's verdict that rows outside the selected range do not affect output and rows inside do
metrics.payload/allocated bytes by phase: split K/V rows, matrix, views, recurrent, latent; headers on their own line
metrics.handoff_traffic_and_identity: allocations and moves across seal → insert → take → resume (I1), and backing-storage identity (I6)
metrics.contract_duplicate_fraction: duplicate K/V bytes over total allocated K/V representation bytes (matrix capacity + views), headers excluded; recurrent and latent state excluded from both

forecasts.quantity: allocated_bytes of K/V row storage (row allocations + matrix capacity), headers excluded
forecasts.claim: canonical/v1 allocates 2× to 3× what row/v1 does for the same conversation
forecasts.forecast: ratio ∈ [2.0, 3.0] on every subject at every phase (payload bytes identical by construction)
forecasts.applies_when: only where the denominator holds non-zero ordinary K/V row storage; a phase or layer with no K/V rows (recurrent-only, latent-only, or before any append) is recorded N/A, never a failed or undefined ratio

forecasts.quantity: store and duplicate traffic per appended row
forecasts.claim: row/v1 adopts the backend's row; canonical/v1 stores it into its matrix and duplicates it into a view
forecasts.forecast: row/v1: 0 row-sized allocations inside append and the stored row's address equals the moved-in row's (adoption, no store copy); canonical/v1: STORE traffic kv_dim × 4 per K and per V (matrix row count grows by one, via its public cache()) and DUPLICATE traffic exactly one row-sized allocation per K and per V (the view), i.e. 8·kv_dim bytes duplicated per position per layer, plus realloc-move traffic ≤ 2× the final matrix bytes over the sequence
forecasts.falsified_if: row/v1 allocates a row or stores at a different address; canonical/v1 duplicates other than exactly one row per K and V per append

forecasts.quantity: rows offered vs kernel selected range, with causal validation
forecasts.claim: sliding layers are lent and hold rows outside their selected range, and those rows do not affect output
forecasts.forecast: rows_offered = n; kernel_selected_range length = min(h+1, w) for sliding layers and h+1 for global layers; held-outside-range fraction at sequence end = max(0, 1 − w/n); I2 holds in both directions on every windowed subject
forecasts.falsified_if: an out-of-range perturbation changes logits, or an in-range one does not
forecasts.not_claimed: that the kernel physically reads exactly the selected range; physical access is not instrumented under the measurement-only rule

forecasts.claim: ConvQkv copies every held K/V row on every call
forecasts.forecast: per conv-QKV layer per call: exactly 2·h row-sized allocations and 2·h·kv_dim·4 bytes of copy traffic (plus two outer Vecs), so a decode of T steps from h₀ totals 8·kv_dim·Σ_{t<T}(h₀+t): quadratic

forecasts.claim: MLA re-derives every latent row on every call
forecasts.forecast: per MLA call: kv_b_proj calls = h + 1 (the held rows plus the one appended this call); batched prefill of n positions: n(n+1)/2
forecasts.falsified_if: kv_b_proj calls per MLA call ≠ h + 1 on the mechanism subject
forecasts.scope: counts on the mechanism subject; real-Kimi magnitude = count × plan geometry, recorded as derived
forecasts.reported_not_adjudicated: the latent-row clone on append (mla.rs:310) is reported from the allocation record as a derived quantity; no instrument isolates it, so it is not part of M5's verdict

forecasts.claim: handoff and resume move state and copy nothing
forecasts.forecast: 0 continuation-sized allocations across seal → insert → take → resume (absorbed_ids excluded), AND every backing allocation's address and capacity identical before seal and after resume (I6)
forecasts.falsified_if: any continuation-sized allocation, or any backing address or capacity changes

forecasts.quantity: contract_duplicate_fraction = duplicate K/V bytes / total allocated K/V representation bytes (matrix capacity + views), headers excluded; recurrent and latent state are outside both numerator and denominator
forecasts.claim: canonical/v1's views are a duplicate that exists only to adapt its matrix authority to &[Vec<f32>]; row/v1's authoritative representation already matches the contract
forecasts.forecast: canonical/v1 ∈ [1/3, 1/2] (views over views + matrix capacity); row/v1 = 0 exactly
forecasts.applies_when: only where the provider holds K/V rows; N/A otherwise (as M1)

forecasts.claim: recurrent state is constant-size and updated in place
forecasts.forecast: recurrent PAYLOAD bytes = the plan's RecurrentGeometry::bytes() (a payload quantity); recurrent ALLOCATED bytes ≥ payload and independent of n; per-call copy traffic = the conv-history buffer only
forecasts.falsified_if: recurrent payload ≠ declared geometry, OR allocated recurrent bytes grow with n, OR observed per-call recurrent operator copy traffic differs from the declared conv-history payload (channels × history length × 4)

controls: positive: the scoped allocator sees canonical/v1's view allocations (non-zero where M2 says non-zero); otherwise row/v1's zero means nothing
negative: with no scope ever opened, attributed allocations are exactly 0
recorder silence: an empty scope (enter → leave with nothing delegated) attributes exactly 0 allocations, proving the instrument does not measure itself
thread integrity: the global scope-active flag records zero foreign-thread allocations on every valid run; a planted allocation on a spawned thread inside a scope marks a test run INVALID
realloc classification: a planted Vec growth that forces a move is counted as move traffic; an in-place one is not
parity: row/v1 and canonical/v1 produce bit-identical logits on every subject (the C3 gate)
I2 has both directions on every windowed subject, sized to the row's scale
I4 reconciliation: row-sized allocations in the ConvQkv interval equal 2·h exactly, or the interval is reported as contaminated
I5: the counting DenseProjections sees every MLA projection (q, kv_a, kv_b, o) with the expected shapes, not only kv_b

outputs.per_subject: a JSON record per subject × provider × phase: geometry, every metric, the controls' verdicts, git SHA, container identity
outputs.adjudication: each forecast HELD / FALSIFIED against the records, stating which byte quantity it used; then a RANKING of avoidable allocated bytes and copy traffic by magnitude on the real containers, each item classified as (a) a duplicate forced by the read contract (VIEW-1's business), (b) an operator implementation choice (a perf rung), or (c) a provider storage choice. VIEW-1 is scoped from (a) only.

out_of_scope: throughput benchmarking — time is recorded only where a copy's cost needs a unit
next: VIEW-1, scoped from the (a) items of MEM-1's ranking; WINDOW-1 after it

byte_quantities.payload_bytes: mathematically live continuation values: elements × dtype size (f32 = 4). Identical across providers for the same conversation; computed from the plan's geometry and the row counts.
byte_quantities.allocated_bytes: live heap capacity attributable to continuation storage: allocations made inside a measured scope and still live, plus the capacity of allocations moved in across the provider boundary (the appended Vec's capacity × 4). Outer-Vec headers and per-row allocation granularity are reported as a separate line, never folded in.
byte_quantities.copy_traffic: bytes written into newly materialised continuation or operator storage: fresh allocations filled from existing continuation values (a row to_vec, a view), plus reallocations the allocator had to MOVE (realloc returning a new address counts the old size; an in-place realloc counts 0). Writing a moved-in value into the provider's authoritative store is reported as STORE traffic, separately from duplicate traffic.

operational_definitions.h: the number of historical rows the provider holds for the layer when the operator call begins (not the token position). Every per-call formula below is written in h.
operational_definitions.n: rows held at the end of the sequence
